title: Uniformizer cone comparison and uniform reduction bound
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $I=(\varpi)$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For any scheme $T$, use the completed coefficient sheaf $A_T=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/I^n)_T$ and the derived module category and canonical reductions of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Let $M\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_T))$, let $a\leq b$ be integers, and suppose $\mathcal H^q(M)=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. For every $n\geq1$, write $M_n=M\otimes^L_{A_T}(A/I^n)_T$ and let $\operatorname{Res}_n M_n$ be its restriction of scalars along $A_T\to(A/I^n)_T$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. There is a natural distinguished triangle
$$M\xrightarrow{\varpi^n\operatorname{id}}M\longrightarrow\operatorname{Res}_n M_n\longrightarrow M[1].$$
Consequently $\mathcal H^q(M_n)=0$ for $q\notin[a-1,b]$, with the same interval for every positive $n$. The triangle is in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_T))$ [def-weil-triangulated-category]; no identification of the constant- and completed-coefficient ambient categories is asserted.

proof.text: Put $R=A_T$, $S=(A/I^n)_T$. The DVR and finite-quotient clauses of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] give $0\to A\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}A\to A/I^n\to0$, with $A$ Noetherian and $A/I^n$ finite. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-module-section-properties] its constant-sheaf sequence is exact. By [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction], $R$ is flat over $\underline A$ and $R\otimes_{\underline A}\underline{A/I^n}\cong S$ canonically (flatness identifies ordinary and derived tensor here). Tensor the sequence by $R$ to obtain $0\to R\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}R\to S\to0$, with quotient map the canonical projection.

proof.text: Choose a K-flat representative $P$ of $M$ as in [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Apply [lem-cbc-regular-quotient-cone-augmentation] to the exact sequence of Step 1, with $r=\varpi^n$. It gives a natural isomorphism $A_M:Q_R C(r\operatorname{id}_P)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_n M_n$. Its component is the quotient augmentation $(y,x)\mapsto y\otimes1$; it carries the cone inclusion to canonical reduction and is independent of representatives, natural for all derived morphisms.

proof.text: The cone-triangle convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] makes $M\xrightarrow{r}M\xrightarrow{i}Q_RC(r\operatorname{id}_P)\xrightarrow{-p}M[1]$ distinguished. Transport its third vertex along $A_M$ from Step 2: the maps become $A_Mi$ and $(-p)A_M^{-1}$. The naturality in [lem-cbc-regular-quotient-cone-augmentation], together with the diagonal cone maps commuting with inclusion and projection, gives the asserted natural triangle.

source.place: Tag 05RU (definition-unbounded-derived-category), with cone triangles; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YU for the K-flat tensor construction.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact], with the functors of [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] preserves the underlying abelian sheaf, hence kernels, images and cohomology, and reflects zero objects. In the exact segment $\mathcal H^q(M)\to\mathcal H^q(\operatorname{Res}_nM_n)\to\mathcal H^{q+1}(M)$, both outer terms vanish when $q<a-1$ or $q>b$. Thus $\mathcal H^q(M_n)=0$ outside $[a-1,b]$. This interval does not depend on the chosen positive $n$.
